brief.topic: A Tree Measured by Its Smaller Companion

s01: A tree can be measured without climbing it.
Its shadow carries a copy of its height, stretched along the ground.
A little upright stick can tell us the scale.
For this moment, sunlight reaches both objects at the same angle.
The ground is level, and both stand upright.
The tree, its shadow, and a ray form a right triangle.
The stick makes a smaller triangle with the same angles.
Enlarge the small triangle until its shadow matches the large one.
Its height must enlarge by the same factor.
This is what similar triangles preserve: ratios between corresponding sides.
Suppose a one-metre stick casts a two-metre shadow.
A ten-metre tree shadow is five times as long.
The tree is therefore five times as tall as the stick: five metres.
We used a comparison, not the exact angle of the sun.
As the sun rises, both shadows shorten.
The ratio between the two heights still matches the ratio between their shadows.
Measure them at the same time, on level ground.
Something difficult to reach can become accessible through a smaller companion.

scenes.narration:
A tree can be measured without climbing it. Its shadow carries a copy of its height, stretched along the ground. A little upright stick can tell us the scale.

For this moment, sunlight reaches both objects at the same angle. The ground is level, and both stand upright. The tree, its shadow, and a ray form a right triangle. The stick makes a smaller triangle with the same angles.

Enlarge the small triangle until its shadow matches the large one. Its height must enlarge by the same factor. This is what similar triangles preserve: ratios between corresponding sides.

Suppose a one-metre stick casts a two-metre shadow. A ten-metre tree shadow is five times as long. The tree is therefore five times as tall as the stick: five metres. We used a comparison, not the exact angle of the sun.

As the sun rises, both shadows shorten. The ratio between the two heights still matches the ratio between their shadows. Measure them at the same time, on level ground. Something difficult to reach can become accessible through a smaller companion.
